public_body: Cotuit Board Of Fire Commissioners Union Negotiation Committee
overall: The AG found no open meeting violation in the Committee's handling of a complaint, since it only forwarded the complaint to counsel, but found improper complaint-response procedure and a late response, and declined the non-OML questions. No orders issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee met, corresponded, or spoke outside a posted meeting to respond to a prior Open Meeting Law complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not discuss the complaint outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Committee responded to a complaint through its attorney within 14 days without first reviewing the allegations at a meeting, which the AG found was improper procedure.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Committee responded to the complaint via its attorney within the required time period, it did so without first reviewing the allegations during a meeting; instead simply forwarding the complaint to legal counsel for response.

allegations.summary: The Committee's response to the instant complaint came six months after filing, well beyond the 14-day deadline; the AG reminded that failing to respond is itself a violation.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we note that the Committee did not respond to the instant complaint until six months after it was filed, well beyond the 14-day requirement of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint also posed questions about hiring a law firm and asked the Committee to schedule a meeting on concerns, without alleging a specific OML violation.
allegations.key_passage: Because this portion of the complaint does not specifically allege any violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to address the questions raised.
